correctness.rationale: The interlacing spline is a common signed extremizer for every cell and mixing law, yielding the exact operator seminorm. Jensen and the exact equality condition determine every pointwise optimizer and weakly continuous Dirac selection attains the global infimum. De Moivre MAD together with strict discrete log-concavity yields all exact parity maxima; Stirling yields the sharp n^(-3/2) constant. The standalone checker independently verifies rational transport, spline identities and all finite candidate comparisons. Finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the exact centered-measure minimax problem, the all-law common Lipschitz extremizer, the full pointwise optimal-measure classification and the parity-sensitive global optimizer. The 2013 binomial MAD identity is explicitly credited to prior work, while the previously proved consecutive Bernstein degree bound is a Bernoulli-jitter corollary not claimed anew. Full-text comparisons of relevant approximation literature found modulus estimates and general kernel definitions but no implication of the constrained sharp optimum. Priority is qualified by partially inaccessible older papers.

value.rationale: A complete sharp minimax classification in a natural family of positive, affine-preserving one-cell refinements. It identifies every pointwise optimal law and a universal extremal function, reveals parity-dependent worst-case sampling bias, and gives an n^(-3/2) optimum sharply better than the n^(-1) scale of conventional cell averaging. The exact MAD identity and prior neighboring-degree result are acknowledged, not relabeled as new.
